# Stealth Notepad — Feature Implementation Plan
<!-- Generated by feature-planner agent from specs 01–04. Status: all 4 specs executed. -->

## Architecture Recap

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `main.js` | Electron main process — window creation, `globalShortcut` registration, IPC listeners, window state |
| `renderer.js` | Browser renderer — DOM manipulation, `ipcRenderer` events, `localStorage` persistence |
| `index.html` | UI markup + inline CSS — frameless dark window, title-bar, textarea, shortcuts-hint bar |
| `native-helper.js` | Stub for Windows capture-exclusion (no native bindings active) |
| `package.json` | `electron ^28`, `electron-builder ^24.9.1`, no runtime dependencies yet |

Key architectural constraints to respect:
- `nodeIntegration: true` + `contextIsolation: false` — `require('electron')` works directly in `renderer.js`
- `-webkit-app-region: drag` on `.title-bar`, `no-drag` on interactive children
- `setContentProtection(true)` on macOS; Windows stub exists in `native-helper.js`
- IPC is one-way for most operations: renderer sends to main (`ipcRenderer.send`), main pushes to renderer (`webContents.send`)

## Feature 1 — Keyboard-based Window Movement

### Overview
Register four global shortcuts (`CommandOrControl+Alt+Left/Right/Up/Down`) in `main.js`. Each press reads the current window position with `mainWindow.getPosition()` and shifts it by 10 px with `mainWindow.setPosition()`. No renderer changes are required — this is entirely a main-process concern.

### Files to modify
- `main.js` — add four `globalShortcut.register` calls inside `registerHotkeys()`

### Key code snippets

**Inside `registerHotkeys()` in `main.js` — append after the ESC block:**

```js
// Ctrl+Alt+Arrow — Move window 10px per press
const MOVE_STEP = 10;

globalShortcut.register('CommandOrControl+Alt+Left', () => {
  if (!mainWindow) return;
  const [x, y] = mainWindow.getPosition();
  mainWindow.setPosition(x - MOVE_STEP, y);
});

globalShortcut.register('CommandOrControl+Alt+Right', () => {
  if (!mainWindow) return;
  const [x, y] = mainWindow.getPosition();
  mainWindow.setPosition(x + MOVE_STEP, y);
});

globalShortcut.register('CommandOrControl+Alt+Up', () => {
  if (!mainWindow) return;
  const [x, y] = mainWindow.getPosition();
  mainWindow.setPosition(x, y - MOVE_STEP);
});

globalShortcut.register('CommandOrControl+Alt+Down', () => {
  if (!mainWindow) return;
  const [x, y] = mainWindow.getPosition();
  mainWindow.setPosition(x, y + MOVE_STEP);
});
```

### Hotkeys / UX
| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Ctrl+Alt+Left | Move window 10 px left |
| Ctrl+Alt+Right | Move window 10 px right |
| Ctrl+Alt+Up | Move window 10 px up |
| Ctrl+Alt+Down | Move window 10 px down |

These are global shortcuts — they fire even when the app does not have keyboard focus (consistent with the existing `Ctrl+Shift+N` toggle pattern). The shortcuts bar in `index.html` should be updated to document them:

```html
<!-- append inside .shortcuts-hint in index.html -->
<span class="shortcut"><span class="key">Ctrl+Alt+&#8592;&#8593;&#8595;&#8594;</span> Move</span>
```

### Edge cases & gotchas
1. **Window off-screen**: `setPosition` happily moves the window off any display. Add optional bounds clamping using `screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workAreaSize` if needed — but for stealth use, off-screen placement may be intentional (hide in corner).
2. **Conflict with system shortcuts**: On macOS, `Ctrl+Alt+Arrow` is used by Mission Control / Spaces by default. Users may need to remap those in System Settings → Keyboard → Shortcuts. Consider documenting this in the README.
3. **`mainWindow` null guard**: Always check `if (!mainWindow)` before calling `getPosition` to avoid crashes after the window is closed.
4. **`movable: true` is already set** in the `BrowserWindow` constructor — no change needed there.
5. **Multi-monitor**: `getPosition()` returns screen coordinates relative to the primary display origin; `setPosition` accepts the same coordinate space. Works correctly across monitors.

### npm dependencies
None. `getPosition()` and `setPosition()` are built into Electron's `BrowserWindow` API.

## Feature 2 — Silent Operations (No `confirm()` Popups)

### Overview
Every `confirm()` call in `renderer.js` blocks the renderer thread and produces a visible native dialog — the opposite of stealth. Replace all two instances with instant, silent actions. The close button sends IPC directly; the clear shortcut clears immediately and fires the existing `showNotification()` toast.

### Files to modify
- `renderer.js` — remove two `confirm()` guards
- `index.html` — no changes required (toast is injected into DOM by `renderer.js`)

### Key code snippets

**Replace the close button handler (lines 25-29 in current `renderer.js`):**

```js
// BEFORE (blocks with native dialog):
closeBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
  if (confirm('Are you sure you want to close Stealth Notepad?')) {
    ipcRenderer.send('close');
  }
});

// AFTER (instant, silent):
closeBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
  ipcRenderer.send('close');
});
```

**Replace the `clear-text` IPC handler (lines 32-38 in current `renderer.js`):**

```js
// BEFORE (blocks with native dialog):
ipcRenderer.on('clear-text', () => {
  if (confirm('Clear all text?')) {
    notepad.value = '';
    localStorage.removeItem('notepad-content');
    showNotification('Text cleared');
  }
});

// AFTER (instant, silent — toast confirms the action non-blockingly):
ipcRenderer.on('clear-text', () => {
  notepad.value = '';
  localStorage.removeItem('notepad-content');
  showNotification('Text cleared');
});
```

The existing `showNotification()` function (lines 50-73) is already a non-blocking, self-removing DOM element — no changes needed there.

### Hotkeys / UX
No hotkey changes. The existing `Ctrl+Shift+C` global shortcut in `main.js` already sends `'clear-text'` to the renderer. The ESC shortcut hides the window. The close button click now quits immediately.

If a "undo clear" affordance is ever desired, store the last value in a module-scoped variable before clearing:

```js
// Optional undo buffer (not required for Feature 2, but a safe extension point):
let lastClearedContent = '';

ipcRenderer.on('clear-text', () => {
  lastClearedContent = notepad.value;
  notepad.value = '';
  localStorage.removeItem('notepad-content');
  showNotification('Text cleared');
});
```

### Edge cases & gotchas
1. **Accidental close**: Removing the confirmation means a mis-click on the red dot quits the app and discards unsaved work. Mitigate by relying on `localStorage` auto-save (already implemented on every `input` event) — the next launch restores content.
2. **Double-fire protection**: The `ipcMain.on('close')` handler calls `app.quit()` which triggers `window-all-closed`. No changes needed there.
3. **macOS Dock bounce**: `app.quit()` from IPC is clean — no lingering processes.
4. **`confirm()` in Electron context**: With `contextIsolation: false`, `confirm()` uses Chromium's built-in synchronous dialog which halts the JS event loop. Its removal also eliminates a subtle performance hazard.

### npm dependencies
None.

## Feature 3 — Opacity Control

### Overview
Cycle window opacity through `[0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0]` on each `Ctrl+Shift+O` press. The index is held in a module-level variable in `main.js`. After each change, send the new opacity value to the renderer via IPC so the title bar can display it. The renderer updates a `<span>` in the title bar text.

### Files to modify
- `main.js` — add opacity state variable, register shortcut, add IPC handler, send opacity event
- `renderer.js` — listen for `'opacity-changed'` IPC event, update title bar span
- `index.html` — add `<span id="opacity-display">` inside `.title`

### Key code snippets

**`main.js` — add at module level (before `createWindow`):**

```js
const OPACITY_LEVELS = [0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0];
let opacityIndex = 3; // default: fully opaque (1.0)
```

**`main.js` — inside `registerHotkeys()`, append after the movement shortcuts:**

```js
// Ctrl+Shift+O — Cycle window opacity
globalShortcut.register('CommandOrControl+Shift+O', () => {
  if (!mainWindow) return;
  opacityIndex = (opacityIndex + 1) % OPACITY_LEVELS.length;
  const opacity = OPACITY_LEVELS[opacityIndex];
  mainWindow.setOpacity(opacity);
  mainWindow.webContents.send('opacity-changed', opacity);
});
```

**`main.js` — add IPC handler so renderer can also query current opacity on load:**

```js
ipcMain.on('get-opacity', (event) => {
  event.reply('opacity-changed', OPACITY_LEVELS[opacityIndex]);
});
```

**`index.html` — modify `.title` div to include the opacity span:**

```html
<!-- BEFORE: -->
<div class="title">🔒 Stealth Notepad</div>

<!-- AFTER: -->
<div class="title">🔒 Stealth Notepad <span id="opacity-display" style="font-size:10px;opacity:0.5;margin-left:6px;"></span></div>
```

Add this CSS rule in the `<style>` block:

```css
#opacity-display {
  font-size: 10px;
  color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.45);
  margin-left: 6px;
  letter-spacing: 0.5px;
}
```

**`index.html` — shortcuts bar, append:**

```html
<span class="shortcut"><span class="key">Ctrl+Shift+O</span> Opacity</span>
```

**`renderer.js` — append at bottom (before or after the `console.log`):**

```js
// Opacity display
const opacityDisplay = document.getElementById('opacity-display');

ipcRenderer.on('opacity-changed', (event, opacity) => {
  if (opacityDisplay) {
    opacityDisplay.textContent = `${Math.round(opacity * 100)}%`;
  }
});

// Request current opacity on load so display is correct from first render
window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
  ipcRenderer.send('get-opacity');
  // existing saved content load is already here — append after it
});
```

Note: The `DOMContentLoaded` handler already exists in `renderer.js` at line 8. Merge the `ipcRenderer.send('get-opacity')` call into that existing handler rather than creating a second one:

```js
window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
  const savedContent = localStorage.getItem('notepad-content');
  if (savedContent) {
    notepad.value = savedContent;
  }
  // Sync opacity display with main process state
  ipcRenderer.send('get-opacity');
});
```

### Hotkeys / UX
| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Ctrl+Shift+O | Cycle opacity: 30% → 50% → 70% → 100% → 30% → ... |

The title bar shows the current opacity percentage (e.g., `100%`) in a muted style. Each cycle step is visible as the window itself changes transparency — no additional confirmation needed.

### Edge cases & gotchas
1. **`setOpacity` availability**: `BrowserWindow.setOpacity()` is supported on Windows and macOS. On Linux it requires a compositing window manager — if unsupported, Electron silently ignores the call. No guard needed but worth documenting.
2. **Opacity vs. `transparent: true`**: The window already has `transparent: true` (the background CSS uses `rgba(0,0,0,0.85)`). `setOpacity` applies an additional multiplier to the entire window including the CSS alpha. At 30% opacity, the effective background alpha becomes `0.85 * 0.3 ≈ 0.255` — barely visible, which is intentional for stealth.
3. **`alwaysOnTop: true` interaction**: Opacity changes do not affect z-order; the window stays on top regardless of opacity level.
4. **State persistence**: `opacityIndex` resets to `3` (100%) on every app launch. If persistence is wanted, save to `app.getPath('userData')` via `electron-store` or a simple JSON file — out of scope for this feature but a clean extension point.
5. **Race condition on load**: The renderer sends `'get-opacity'` in `DOMContentLoaded`. The main process must have registered `ipcMain.on('get-opacity')` before this fires — it will because `registerHotkeys()` and IPC setup run during `createWindow()` which completes before the renderer's `DOMContentLoaded` event.

### npm dependencies
None. `BrowserWindow.setOpacity()` is a built-in Electron API.

## Feature 4 — Collaborative Room (Socket.IO)

### Overview
Add a lightweight Socket.IO server (`server.js`) that manages named rooms. The Electron renderer connects to this server as a Socket.IO client. Users can create a room (generates a 6-char alphanumeric ID), share the ID with a collaborator who joins it, and from that point every `input` event on the textarea is broadcast to all room members — last-write-wins, full value sync. The UI gains a room section in the shortcuts bar: room ID display, copy button, and a connection status dot. The hotkey `Ctrl+Shift+R` creates a new room.

### Files to modify
- `server.js` — new file (Socket.IO server, ~80 lines)
- `main.js` — spawn `server.js` as a child process on app start; add `Ctrl+Shift+R` shortcut; add IPC handlers for create/join/leave
- `renderer.js` — Socket.IO client connection, room creation/join logic, textarea sync, UI updates
- `index.html` — room UI section in shortcuts bar, connection status dot, join modal/inline input
- `package.json` — add `socket.io` (server) and `socket.io-client` (renderer) as runtime dependencies

### Key code snippets

#### `server.js` (new file — place in project root)

```js
// server.js — Socket.IO collaboration server for Stealth Notepad
'use strict';

const { createServer } = require('http');
const { Server } = require('socket.io');

const PORT = process.env.COLLAB_PORT || 4242;

const httpServer = createServer();
const io = new Server(httpServer, {
  cors: { origin: '*' }
});

// rooms: Map<roomId, Set<socketId>>
const rooms = new Map();

function generateRoomId() {
  const chars = 'ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789'; // unambiguous charset
  let id = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
    id += chars[Math.floor(Math.random() * chars.length)];
  }
  return id;
}

io.on('connection', (socket) => {
  let currentRoom = null;

  socket.on('create-room', (callback) => {
    // Leave any previous room
    if (currentRoom) {
      socket.leave(currentRoom);
      const members = rooms.get(currentRoom);
      if (members) members.delete(socket.id);
    }

    let roomId;
    do {
      roomId = generateRoomId();
    } while (rooms.has(roomId));

    rooms.set(roomId, new Set([socket.id]));
    currentRoom = roomId;
    socket.join(roomId);

    if (typeof callback === 'function') callback({ ok: true, roomId });
  });

  socket.on('join-room', (roomId, callback) => {
    const id = (roomId || '').toUpperCase().trim();
    if (!rooms.has(id)) {
      if (typeof callback === 'function') callback({ ok: false, error: 'Room not found' });
      return;
    }

    // Leave any previous room
    if (currentRoom && currentRoom !== id) {
      socket.leave(currentRoom);
      const members = rooms.get(currentRoom);
      if (members) members.delete(socket.id);
    }

    rooms.get(id).add(socket.id);
    currentRoom = id;
    socket.join(id);

    if (typeof callback === 'function') callback({ ok: true, roomId: id });
  });

  socket.on('text-update', (data) => {
    // data: { roomId, content }
    if (!data || data.roomId !== currentRoom) return;
    // Broadcast to everyone else in the room
    socket.to(currentRoom).emit('text-update', { content: data.content });
  });

  socket.on('leave-room', () => {
    if (currentRoom) {
      socket.leave(currentRoom);
      const members = rooms.get(currentRoom);
      if (members) {
        members.delete(socket.id);
        if (members.size === 0) rooms.delete(currentRoom);
      }
      currentRoom = null;
    }
  });

  socket.on('disconnect', () => {
    if (currentRoom) {
      const members = rooms.get(currentRoom);
      if (members) {
        members.delete(socket.id);
        if (members.size === 0) rooms.delete(currentRoom);
      }
    }
  });
});

httpServer.listen(PORT, '127.0.0.1', () => {
  console.log(`[stealth-collab] server listening on 127.0.0.1:${PORT}`);
});
```

const { spawn } = require('child_process');

let collabServer = null;

function startCollabServer() {
  const serverPath = path.join(__dirname, 'server.js');
  collabServer = spawn(process.execPath, [serverPath], {
    env: { ...process.env, COLLAB_PORT: '4242' },

  collabServer.on('error', (err) => {
    console.error('[collab] Failed to start server:', err);

}

#### `renderer.js` — Socket.IO client logic

**Append to the bottom of `renderer.js`:**

```js
// ─── Collaboration (Feature 4) ───────────────────────────────────────────────

// Dynamically load socket.io-client from the local node_modules
// so it works without a bundler
const { io: socketIo } = require('socket.io-client');

const COLLAB_SERVER = 'http://127.0.0.1:4242';

let socket = null;
let activeRoomId = null;
let isSyncing = false; // prevent echo loop

// DOM refs
const connDot = document.getElementById('conn-dot');
const roomIdDisplay = document.getElementById('room-id-display');
const copyRoomBtn = document.getElementById('copy-room-btn');
const createRoomBtn = document.getElementById('create-room-btn');
const joinInput = document.getElementById('join-input');
const joinRoomBtn = document.getElementById('join-room-btn');
const leaveRoomBtn = document.getElementById('leave-room-btn');

function setConnStatus(status) {
  // status: 'disconnected' | 'connecting' | 'connected' | 'error'
  connDot.className = 'conn-dot';
  if (status === 'connected') connDot.classList.add('connected');
  else if (status === 'connecting') connDot.classList.add('connecting');
  else if (status === 'error') connDot.classList.add('error');
  connDot.title = status.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + status.slice(1);
}

function connectSocket() {
  if (socket && socket.connected) return socket;

  setConnStatus('connecting');
  socket = socketIo(COLLAB_SERVER, {
    transports: ['websocket'],
    reconnectionAttempts: 5,
    timeout: 3000
  });

  socket.on('connect', () => setConnStatus('connected'));
  socket.on('disconnect', () => {
    setConnStatus('disconnected');
    if (activeRoomId) {
      activeRoomId = null;
      updateRoomUI(null);
    }
  });
  socket.on('connect_error', () => setConnStatus('error'));

  // Receive text updates from room peers
  socket.on('text-update', ({ content }) => {
    if (isSyncing) return;
    isSyncing = true;
    notepad.value = content;
    localStorage.setItem('notepad-content', content);
    isSyncing = false;
  });

  return socket;
}

function updateRoomUI(roomId) {
  if (roomId) {
    roomIdDisplay.textContent = roomId;
    copyRoomBtn.style.display = 'inline-block';
    leaveRoomBtn.style.display = 'inline-block';
    createRoomBtn.style.display = 'none';
    joinInput.classList.remove('visible');
    joinRoomBtn.style.display = 'none';
  } else {
    roomIdDisplay.textContent = '';
    copyRoomBtn.style.display = 'none';
    leaveRoomBtn.style.display = 'none';
    createRoomBtn.style.display = 'inline-block';
    joinRoomBtn.style.display = 'inline-block';
  }
}

function createRoom() {
  const s = connectSocket();
  s.emit('create-room', (response) => {
    if (response && response.ok) {
      activeRoomId = response.roomId;
      updateRoomUI(activeRoomId);
      showNotification(`Room created: ${activeRoomId}`);
    } else {
      showNotification('Failed to create room');
    }
  });
}

function joinRoom(roomId) {
  const id = (roomId || '').toUpperCase().trim();
  if (!id || id.length !== 6) {
    showNotification('Enter a valid 6-char room ID');
    return;
  }
  const s = connectSocket();
  s.emit('join-room', id, (response) => {
    if (response && response.ok) {
      activeRoomId = response.roomId;
      updateRoomUI(activeRoomId);
      showNotification(`Joined room: ${activeRoomId}`);
    } else {
      showNotification(response ? response.error : 'Room not found');
    }
  });
}

function leaveRoom() {
  if (socket && activeRoomId) {
    socket.emit('leave-room');
  }
  activeRoomId = null;
  updateRoomUI(null);
  showNotification('Left room');
}

// Button event listeners
createRoomBtn.addEventListener('click', createRoom);

joinRoomBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const val = joinInput.value.trim();
  if (val) {
    joinRoom(val);
  } else {
    joinInput.classList.toggle('visible');
    if (joinInput.classList.contains('visible')) joinInput.focus();
  }
});

joinInput.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  if (e.key === 'Enter') joinRoom(joinInput.value);
  if (e.key === 'Escape') joinInput.classList.remove('visible');
});

leaveRoomBtn.addEventListener('click', leaveRoom);

copyRoomBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
  if (activeRoomId) {
    clipboard.writeText(activeRoomId);
    showNotification('Room ID copied!');
  }
});

// Broadcast textarea changes to room peers
notepad.addEventListener('input', () => {
  localStorage.setItem('notepad-content', notepad.value);
  if (socket && socket.connected && activeRoomId && !isSyncing) {
    socket.emit('text-update', { roomId: activeRoomId, content: notepad.value });
  }
});

// IPC: Ctrl+Shift+R hotkey from main process triggers room creation
ipcRenderer.on('create-room', () => {
  createRoom();
});

// Initialise UI state
updateRoomUI(null);
setConnStatus('disconnected');
```

**Important**: The `notepad.addEventListener('input', ...)` block that already exists in `renderer.js` (line 16-18) only saves to `localStorage`. The collab block above replaces that handler with one that does both. Remove or merge the original handler to avoid double-firing:

```js
// REMOVE this from renderer.js (original lines 16-18):
notepad.addEventListener('input', () => {
  localStorage.setItem('notepad-content', notepad.value);
});

// The collab section's input listener (shown above) covers localStorage save + socket emit.
```

### Hotkeys / UX
| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Ctrl+Shift+R | Create a new collaboration room instantly |
| Click `+ Room` | Same as hotkey |
| Click `Join` | Reveals 6-char input field; Enter confirms |
| Click `Copy ID` | Copies room ID to clipboard |
| Click `Leave` | Exits room, stops sync |

The connection status dot in the room bar:
- Grey = not connected to server
- Yellow = connecting
- Green (pulsing) = connected
- Red = connection error

### Edge cases & gotchas
1. **Server not running when user opens app**: `connectSocket()` is called lazily — only when the user first tries to create/join a room. If the server process hasn't started yet (startup race), `connect_error` fires and the dot turns red. Set a small retry in socket.io client options (`reconnectionAttempts: 5`, `reconnectionDelay: 500`) to handle this.

2. **Child process vs. external server**: The plan spawns `server.js` as a child of the Electron main process using `process.execPath` (the Electron binary itself) with `[serverPath]` as the script argument. This works because Electron ships Node.js. If the app is packaged with `electron-builder`, `server.js` must be included in the `files` array of `package.json` build config:
   ```json
   "files": ["main.js", "renderer.js", "index.html", "native-helper.js", "server.js"]
   ```

3. **Port conflict**: Port 4242 may be in use. Add a fallback: try ports 4242–4250 in sequence, or use `0` (OS-assigned) and pass the actual port back to the renderer via an IPC message from the main process after the server emits its `listen` callback.

4. **Last-write-wins race**: If two users type simultaneously, the one whose `text-update` arrives last overwrites the other. This is acceptable for a lightweight stealth notepad. A CRDT (e.g., `yjs`) would be the upgrade path for true conflict-free sync.

5. **`socket.io-client` in renderer with `nodeIntegration: true`**: Because `contextIsolation: false` and `nodeIntegration: true`, `require('socket.io-client')` works directly in `renderer.js` exactly like in a Node script. No bundler (webpack/vite) is needed.

6. **Echo loop prevention**: When the renderer receives a `text-update` from the server and sets `notepad.value`, that assignment does NOT fire the `input` event (only user-initiated input does in browsers). The `isSyncing` guard is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard and can be kept for clarity.

7. **Room ID case sensitivity**: The server stores IDs in uppercase; `join-room` normalises the input with `.toUpperCase()` before emitting. The input field has `text-transform: uppercase` CSS for visual consistency.

8. **Cleanup on app quit**: `collabServer.kill()` in `will-quit` sends SIGTERM to the Node server child process. On Windows, `child_process.kill()` is abrupt (SIGKILL equivalent) — acceptable here since the server holds no disk state.

9. **`socket.io-client` version compatibility**: Install `socket.io@4.x` and `socket.io-client@4.x` together. Mixing major versions (e.g., server v4, client v3) breaks the handshake. Pin both to the same major in `package.json`.

### npm dependencies

```bash
npm install socket.io socket.io-client
```

Add to `package.json` `dependencies` (not `devDependencies`, since these are needed at runtime):
```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "socket.io": "^4.7.5",
    "socket.io-client": "^4.7.5"
  }
}
```

`socket.io-client` must also be available to the renderer. Because the app uses `require()` directly (no bundler), it will resolve from `node_modules` at runtime — this works with `nodeIntegration: true`.

## Summary Table

| Feature | Main Process Changes | Renderer Changes | HTML Changes | New Files | New npm Deps |
|---------|---------------------|-----------------|--------------|-----------|--------------|
| 1. Window Movement | `registerHotkeys()` — 4 shortcuts | None | Shortcuts hint bar label | None | None |
| 2. Silent Ops | None | Remove 2x `confirm()` | None | None | None |
| 3. Opacity Control | Module var + 1 shortcut + 1 IPC handler | 1 IPC listener + title update | Opacity span + CSS | None | None |
| 4. Collab Room | Spawn server child process + 1 shortcut + cleanup | Socket.IO client, full room logic, input handler merge | Room section UI + CSS | `server.js` | `socket.io`, `socket.io-client` |

## Recommended Implementation Order
1. Feature 2 (Silent Ops) — smallest change, immediate quality improvement, zero risk
2. Feature 1 (Window Movement) — pure main.js addition, no renderer changes
3. Feature 3 (Opacity) — minor main + renderer + HTML changes, builds on IPC pattern already established
4. Feature 4 (Collab Room) — largest scope, requires new dependency install and new file; implement last to avoid disrupting working features
